catalog.title: The Mapmaker's Trick
catalog.text: Old mapmakers had a problem: their maps were expensive to survey but cheap to copy. A rival could reprint the same roads and rivers and undersell them. So some mapmakers invented a defense. They added a street that did not exist — a short lane with an invented name, tucked between two real ones. If that lane later turned up on a competitor's map, there was only one possible explanation: the competitor had copied rather than surveyed. These inventions are called trap streets. Modern digital maps still carry the occasional trap, and mapmakers rarely admit which entries are the fakes.

catalog.title: The Meteor Shower
catalog.text: A meteor shower is not really a storm of rocks falling toward Earth. It is Earth driving through a trail of old dust. Comets shed grit as they swing near the Sun, leaving a stream of it along their orbit. Friction heats the air around each grain until it glows. The streak you see is not the rock burning; it is the column of hot air left behind it.
